subject.title: perf(sqlite): memory-map reads on local-filesystem databases (#112758)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a global 256 MiB mmap ceiling for every local-WAL SQLite connection, or require a smaller/budgeted default after multi-handle RSS validation?
rationale: The patch changes a runtime default for all local state databases, while the appropriate trade-off between synchronous read latency and RSS-driven diagnostics is a product and operational policy choice rather than a mechanically determined fix.

options.title: Validate and bound before merge
options.body: Measure representative local multi-database usage against the memory diagnostics thresholds, then use the largest default that stays within the intended process budget.

options.title: Accept the 256 MiB default
options.body: Merge the performance-oriented ceiling as proposed and explicitly accept the potential RSS and diagnostic-work trade-off for local deployments.

options.title: Defer global mmap enablement
options.body: Keep the current default until a broader SQLite memory-budget policy or a narrower owner-specific implementation is agreed.

recommendation.title: Validate and bound before merge
recommendation.body: Measure representative local multi-database usage against the memory diagnostics thresholds, then use the largest default that stays within the intended process budget.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior work and production report cover the specific NFS/SIGBUS safety constraint that this change relies on; ownership of the final global memory-budget decision remains ambiguous.
